name: Production food database target and configuration decision packet
phase: Discovery and owner decision support only
purpose: Present a concrete recommended initial Home Cottage configuration and separately gated execution plan. Recommendations are not owner selections or execution approvals.

topologyComparison.option: A: one dedicated shared food database
topologyComparison.implementation: Existing constructors accept the same FoodD1Database object; Q supplies exact reads. No repository change required.
topologyComparison.configuration: One new binding/target, one food migration directory and one target verification/recovery plan.
topologyComparison.migrations: Existing migrations/food stream: 0001 then 0002, with no file renaming.
topologyComparison.operations: Simpler initial operation, but both food domains share database availability, capacity and recovery failure domains.
topologyComparison.transactions: Internal menu publication integrity remains transactional. Shared storage does not make separate FOOD-001 reads and menu writes one transaction or an atomic cross-repository snapshot.
topologyComparison.isolation: Dedicated from commerce/CRM/Sesh/identity, with FOOD-001 and FOOD-002 table families together; no independent infrastructure isolation between those two families.
topologyComparison.scalability: Shares capacity; no capacity sufficiency claim is made without later workload evidence.
topologyComparison.futureSplit: Injection and absence of cross-family SQL foreign keys permit a later split. Actual data transfer, canonical-history verification, exact-reference checks and cutover require a separately approved migration project; not an automatic switch.

topologyComparison.option: B: separate dedicated FOOD-001 and FOOD-002 databases
topologyComparison.implementation: Existing H/J/L accept Q reads sourced independently from menu storage. I acquires one explicitly selected database; a trusted call site acquires each source separately using existing capabilities. No new generic abstraction is required.
topologyComparison.configuration: Two approved binding keys/targets and explicit environment mapping; greater configuration and recovery complexity.
topologyComparison.migrations: Independent streams are possible, but both current SQL files share migrations/food. An approved split-stream plan is needed before assigning directories or applying files; do not apply the entire directory blindly to both targets.
topologyComparison.operations: Independent capacity/recovery boundaries, but menu operations verifying FOOD-001 references still depend on both databases being available.
topologyComparison.transactions: No cross-database transaction or physical FOOD-002-to-FOOD-001 FK; logical exact-read validation remains authoritative.
topologyComparison.isolation: Stronger operational separation at the cost of coordinating backups and consistent reference recovery.
topologyComparison.scalability: Independent workload allocation is possible; no current measured need establishes this extra complexity.
topologyComparison.futureSplit: Already separated; still requires coordinated historical-reference preservation and no latest substitution.

recommendation.topology: Option A: one new dedicated shared food D1 database for initial Home Cottage launch
recommendation.rationale: RIVER_FOOD_DB matches existing RIVER_*_DB conventions and FOOD-001F/H contract, has no committed collision, and serves both repositories. river-food follows river-commerce/river-crm/river-identity resource naming. The existing migration directory supports shared storage directly.
recommendation.approvalStatus: RECOMMENDATION ONLY; topology, name, account/environment/location and actual target remain owner-unselected. Resource availability has not been queried. If the proposed name is unavailable, return to owner selection instead of silently choosing another target.

futureFiles.runtimeEffect: Changes runtime binding availability on deployment

otherFileDecisions: No existing domain/repository/runtime interface, migration SQL, new environment schema, package script or generic handler wrapper needs modification for the recommended plan. Any later local/dev config or origin-config file must be explicitly selected, not silently created. No source contains concrete administrator values.
bindingPreviewRules: Documentary shape only, not usable configuration. No fabricated UUID or existing unrelated ID. Local persistence is a separately selected isolated directory; preview_database_id is optional only after a distinct preview target is approved/provisioned. Do not point preview/dev at production by default. Named Wrangler environments must be explicitly configured before using --env; bindings cannot be assumed inherited.

futureCommands.verificationBasis: Installed Wrangler CLI help for d1 create, d1 migrations apply/list and d1 execute was inspected with --help only; no infrastructure command executed.
futureCommands.createGate: OWNER APPROVAL REQUIRED — CREATES CLOUD INFRASTRUCTURE. Verify authenticated account, target environment and location/jurisdiction decision first; add approved --location or --jurisdiction only if selected. Capture returned database UUID and suggested binding block privately for owner verification. --update-config=false separates creation from config editing. Name is substituted if owner chooses another name.
futureCommands.localApply: npx wrangler d1 migrations apply RIVER_FOOD_DB --local --persist-to <approved-isolated-local-state-directory> --config <approved-local-test-config>
futureCommands.localList: npx wrangler d1 migrations list RIVER_FOOD_DB --local --persist-to <approved-isolated-local-state-directory> --config <approved-local-test-config>
futureCommands.remoteList: npx wrangler d1 migrations list RIVER_FOOD_DB --remote --config <verified-target-config>
futureCommands.remoteApply: npx wrangler d1 migrations apply RIVER_FOOD_DB --remote --config <verified-target-config>
futureCommands.remoteGate: OWNER APPROVAL REQUIRED — CHANGES PERSISTENT DATABASE SCHEMA. Immediately verify account, binding/name/UUID, environment, migration inventory and backup/recovery plan. CLI confirmation is not owner authorization; noninteractive CLI may skip confirmation. No --yes or unattended execution is authorized here.
futureCommands.schemaInventory: npx wrangler d1 execute RIVER_FOOD_DB --remote --config <verified-target-config> --command "SELECT type,name,tbl_name,sql FROM sqlite_schema WHERE name LIKE 'food_%' ORDER BY type,name" --json
futureCommands.inventoryGate: Future read-only configured access still requires approval and exact target verification. Local equivalent uses --local and approved --persist-to; never omit target mode.
futureCommands.administratorGate: Separately approve canonical principal verification and secret configuration. Supply the approved value through the prompt; do not put it in command arguments or Git.
futureCommands.deployment: npm run build followed by npm run deploy; package publish combines these and release includes publish, so neither publish nor release is a harmless validation command.
futureCommands.environmentFlags: Append --env <approved-named-environment> only when that named environment exists and its exact target has been verified. Templates are descriptions, not instructions to execute in this slice.

migrationPlan.application: One approved migrations apply invocation processes unapplied files in the configured stream; inspect pending list first to ensure exactly intended inventory. No renumbering or direct execute bypass of migration tracking.
levels: Existing isolated Miniflare SQL tests validate semantics without configured databases
Separately approved local migration application uses dedicated temporary configuration/state
Separately approved remote application changes the verified cloud target
verification: Migration list reports no intended pending files; distinguish pending list from complete applied-history proof.

Read sqlite_schema and compare exact eight food tables against 0001/0002, all UPDATE/DELETE rejection triggers, stable-offer and publication-membership triggers, indexes, safe-integer checks and exact composite FKs.
Approved read-only foreign-key/schema checks show required constraints and no integrity violations; required repository reads decode correctly and absent exact coordinates remain not-found.

Exercise mutation/concurrency/rollback smoke tests in isolated local harness/state. Production writes are not non-destructive verification and require a separate approved data plan; do not insert test products merely to prove production schema.
Record target, migration output and verification evidence without publishing identifiers/secrets. Successful local tests do not establish remote replication or production transport guarantees.
migrationPlan.partialFailure: Installed apply help states a failing migration rolls back while earlier successful migrations remain applied. Do not assume the whole two-file stream rolls back atomically; inspect actual target state before forward correction.

administratorDecision.item: Select/verify the principal that owns Home Cottage private menu administration
administratorDecision.source: Owner-approved active canonical PrincipalId in existing identity system; protected per-environment trusted configuration under RIVER_FOOD_ADMIN_PRINCIPAL_ID as recommended by FOOD-001H.
administratorDecision.secretMeaning: Privileged configuration, not a credential. Recommend secret storage rather than committing the value; secrecy never replaces fresh session/principal authorization.
administratorDecision.wiring: Future trusted call site parses unchanged through parsePrincipalId then injects administratorPrincipalId into J. J does not acquire this key automatically.
administratorDecision.missing: Fixed sanitized configuration-unavailable/503, zero mutation/body consumption and no inferred/default/request-supplied identity.

originDecision.source: Recommend approved canonical production origin derived from the trusted site configuration already declared in astro.config.mjs, through an explicit reviewed server configuration mapping. Dev/test mappings remain separate.
originDecision.selection: Owner confirms the intended canonical origin and how it is supplied to M; no new origin environment key or concrete value is selected by S.
originDecision.rules: Validate canonical origin without deriving trust from incoming Origin, Host or request.url. Existing site is a candidate, not automatic food activation approval. Missing/noncanonical source returns fixed sanitized configuration 503 before body read; no fallback.

sessionIdentity.status: ALREADY RESOLVED — REUSE EXISTING SESSION/IDENTITY PATH
sessionIdentity.flow: Astro APIRoute context.session -> J new AstroPrincipalSessionStore(session, optional clock), new D1PrincipalRepository(environment.RIVER_IDENTITY_DB), new DefaultSessionPrincipalResolver({ sessions, principals }); shared async session compatibility remains unchanged.
sessionIdentity.selection: No new identity binding or session abstraction required. Existing identity target must be available and intended administrator verified separately; declaration is not live-health proof. Fresh request-scoped components prevent session state leakage.

runtimeAssembly: Obtain trusted Cloudflare env using existing endpoint precedent; obtain request-scoped context.session.
acquirePrivateFoodMenuDatabaseFromEnvironment({ environment, bindingName: approved RIVER_FOOD_DB key }); verify result before further construction.

createPrivateFoodMenuOperationRuntimeFromServerContext({ environment, bindingName: same approved key, session, readDependencies, administratorPrincipalId, now?: trustedClock }); J/L internally create D1FoodMenuRepository with the same environment database object and one private service/workspace/gate bundle.
createPrivateFoodMenuMutationRequestAdapter({ boundary }); createPrivateFoodMenuMutationServerHandler({ adapter }); handler.handle(context.request), with O response mapping inside P.
runtimeRules: Only a future concrete call site is needed; no new composition abstraction. Construction stays synchronous/I/O-free. Gate precedes lazy body parsing and normal mutation reauthorizes. Missing trusted database/admin/origin causes fixed sanitized no-store JSON 503 at assembly boundary, not a new M result or P callback failure. No memory/unrelated database fallback.

routeReadiness.configuration: Not ready: binding, admin and trusted-origin configuration absent/unselected.

recommendedSequence: Owner reviews topology/binding/resource/environment/admin-origin sourcing and records selections; no selection authorizes execution.
Prepare sanitized configuration patch preview and local test/recovery plan without modifying active config or inventing database IDs.
Separately approve and create dedicated shared D1 target; verify captured ID/account/environment.
Separately approve binding declaration with real verified ID and migrations/food; regenerate types and review exact diff before any deployment.
Run approved isolated/local validation, then separately approve remote application of 0001 followed by 0002; inspect actual schema non-destructively.
Separately approve administrator verification/configuration and trusted canonical-origin mapping; preserve existing session/identity path.
Privately validate runtime assembly and policy/auth/mutation behavior in isolated tests without production fixtures.
Separately approve thin route source registration and validate build/security/fail-closed behavior.
Separately approve deployment, recognizing it exposes registered route source; activation approval must be obtained before live functionality is enabled, not deferred until after exposure.
Perform separately approved private post-deployment checks and monitor sanitized failures; public commerce/sales activation remains outside this plan.

recovery.plan: Leave an unused dedicated database intact if later phases halt; no automatic deletion or destructive cleanup. Creation does not activate access.
Disable food route use, restore reviewed prior config/protected settings and redeploy only with approval; preserve data and avoid fallback to other targets.

Verify backup/recovery before execution, inspect partially applied state on failure and prefer forward correction. Git revert does not undo schema. Append-only triggers/history remain preserved; no routine drops or destructive rollback.
Withdraw/disable endpoint or redeploy reviewed prior commit with owner approval, preserve append-only database history and revalidate identity/origin/target before reactivation.

immediateNextStep: After owner review and recorded selections, prepare a configuration patch PREVIEW only using unresolved ID placeholders outside active config. Actual D1 provisioning follows only a separate explicit cloud-infrastructure approval; no further generic architecture specification or wrapper is needed.
